text:
Ken: heads-up — the rerank endpoint (embed+rerank lane) started firing throttles around 09:12 UTC, seeing a spike in 429s and queue depth on eu-west-1 gpu pool. p50 fine, p95/p99 climbing.
ops-bot: [ALERT] capacity-lane: embed-rerank saturated on eu-west-1-gpu-pool-2. admission_control::engaged -> rejecting low-priority requests.
Lucy: copying logs now. any recent deploys to rerank service?
Ken: no deploys. config change from last week to split embed vs rerank lanes, but that was unchanged. looks like a traffic pattern shift — batch sizes up + some big idempotent rerank jobs kicked off.
Arjun: can we get a sample of the queue drain and the admission decisions? run: `rctl inspect queues --service=rerank --lane=embed-rerank --window=10m`
Ken: pasted output: ```
# rctl inspect output (trimmed)
lane: embed-rerank
pool: eu-west-1-gpu-pool-2
queued: 128 -> 340 (10m)
active_infers: 46
throttled(reqs/s): 210 -> 430
p95_latency(ms): 420 -> 930
admission: reject if queued > 120 && fair_share_low_prio
```
Devon: that queued -> 340 is huge. We have two levers: 1) spill low-priority rerank to cpu-best-effort lane, 2) increase lane capacity (spin up more GPU nodes). Both have tradeoffs (latency vs cost).
Priya: cost estimate for +2 nodes in eu-west-1-gpu-pool-2 is ~+8% on that cluster, ~+1.2% company-wide for a week. If this is a transient traffic burst, we should avoid autoscaling to save cost.
Arjun: propose intermediate: adjust admission control to apply a stricter fair-share with per-customer windowing so heavy customers don't starve the rest. Example patch to admission policy: ```
# admission.yaml (snippet)
policies:
  - name: fair_share_window
    type: sliding_window
    window_s: 60
    per_customer_share: 0.25
    low_prio_spill_to: cpu-best-effort
    enqueue_threshold: 100
    reject_threshold: 200
```
Lucy: quick question — spill_to cpu-best-effort will increase end-to-end latency for those requests; are we ok with SLOs being broken for batch rerank jobs?
Devon: acceptable for low-priority/async rerank jobs, not for interactive search rerank. We need tags on requests so admission can distinguish interactive vs batch. Are request tagging and routing working?
Ken: yes, we already have `priority: interactive|batch` metadata. The issue is the large number of batch reranks not being tagged correctly by an upstream job — adding a fallback tag would help.
ops-bot: [LOG] recent top offenders by rate: customer-acme (42% of embed-rerank reqs), backup-indexer-job (18%), internal-loadtest (7%).
Priya: If acme is 42%, throttling them or asking them to backoff seems reasonable. Can account team pause heavy jobs or do a negotiated limit?
Arjun: short-term mitigations: 1) enforce per-customer cap in admission (fast), 2) enable spillover for requests tagged `batch`, 3) notify account team and ask to throttle back. Medium-term: implement dynamic fair-share that adapts based on observed latency injection.
Lucy: I'm going to flip the admission threshold to reject_threshold=220 and enable spill_to for `batch` only. Will monitor for 15m.
Ken: noted. can we also temporarily bump the per-request concurrency for interactive to preserve p99? i.e., reserve 20% of lane capacity for `interactive` with strict preemption.
Devon: yes, reservation change is safe: `rctl set-lane-reservation embed-rerank --interactive=0.2`
Ken: doing it now.
Ken: done — reservation set, admission thresholds updated, and CPU spillover enabled for batch.
ops-bot: [ACTION] admission-policy updated by Lucy at 09:28 UTC.
Lucy: monitoring dashboards — p99 latency for interactive fell back from 930ms -> 310ms within 90s. queue depth trending down from 340 -> 120.
Arjun: good. next steps: we need a follow-up ticket to (a) add per-customer auto-throttle with backoff headers, (b) validate upstream tagging for batch jobs, (c) run a cost analysis for autoscale triggers vs short-term throttles. I'll file it.
Priya: tagging account team to coordinate with acme on rate limits. @sales-engagement please do a quick FYI.
Ken: final note — let's add a short runbook item: when embed-rerank sees sustained queued > 150 for 5m, prefer fair-share + spillover before spinning GPUs. Saves cost and reduces noisy neighbor risk.
Lucy: added runbook entry and linked incident. :thumbsup:
Devon: thanks everyone — keeping an eye on eu-west pool for next 24h. :eyes:
